newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-GILCHRIST CANES WEST INDIES BOWLERS.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-GILCHRIST CANES WEST INDIES BOWLERS.

text.p: Wicketkeeper Adam Gilchrist piled the pressure on Australia test counterpart Ian Healy with an unbeaten century for Western Australia in their three-day tour match against West Indies on Friday.
Gilchrist, who was called up as a replacement for an injured Healy during Austrlia's recent tour to India, scored 108 not out before declaring the home side's first innings on 293 for six.
Gilchrist, acting Western Australia captain in the absence of injured Tom Moody, is widely regarded as the most serious challenger for Healy's test place.
In an aggressive innings, Gilchrist smashed 14 boundaries and three sixes, reaching his century in 98 balls.
At close of play on the first day at the WACA, West Indies were 53 for one after losing opener Adrian Griffith for nine.
Opener Robert Samuels remained unbeaten on 26 alongside number three Shivnarine Chanderpaul on 11 not out.
Gilchrist came to the crease with the total on 152 for four and was particularly severe on West Indies' fast bowler Kenneth Benjamin, who finished wicketless after conceding 74 runs in 17 overs.
The tourists went into the match without vice-captain and star batsman Brian Lara, who was rested. Fast bowler Nixon McLean was ruled out with a troublesome groin injury.
Western Australia opener Mark Lavender anchored the home side's innings, contributing a watchful 51.
Spinner Carl Hooper offered some encouragement for the tourists by taking three for 64 from 19 overs.
West Indies will face Australia in the first test in Brisbane, starting on November 22.
